subject: Meridian Health renewal — rate matrix, provisional price-hold, and capacity ladder
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Meridian Health renewal — initial rate planning

Hi Laura,

Hope you're well — thought it was a good time to start aligning on Meridian's upcoming renewal so Finance has runway for the FY28 budget cycle. We currently see Meridian on our Standard Commitment tier with a mix of burst and reserved capacity. Before I put together formal options, two quick asks: 1) do you have a target % discount or effective rate that Finance is aiming for? 2) any anticipated change to peak seq length / embedding-heavy usage next year (we saw some uptick in Q1).

Goal: propose a simple rate matrix with a provisional price-hold through your procurement review (we can do a 60-day hold tied to signature). If that sounds useful I can draft a matrix with step levels for 1) committed monthly token volume, 2) on-demand burst uplift pricing, and 3) an onboarding credit to smooth month-one spikes.

If it's helpful I can loop in Monica for usage and an ops summary; Grace can run the pricing levers and model the effective blended rate. Let me know a couple slots and I'll put a 30-min call on both our calendars.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0173

--

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@meridianhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <t.alvarez@meridianhealth.com>, procurement@meridianhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-06T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meridian Health renewal — initial rate planning

Sean — thanks for the outreach. High level: Finance has signaled a target of roughly 18-22% reduction in unit rate vs our current blended spend if we commit to a 12-month term. Two important constraints from procurement: any price-hold must be time-bound (they prefer 45-75 days) and tied to a specific SOW or commitment schedule; also we need clearer SLAs for sustained burst > 1.5x baseline.

On usage: Q2-Q3 will see heavier embedding usage as we ramp a new triage classifier (expect +30-40% embeddings by Aug). Peak sequence lengths should remain similar (mostly short prompts).

Tom and procurement are looped. We'd like a simple matrix with committed monthly token buckets, an onboard credit, and a defined burst pricing ladder. If you can send a draft before EOD Wednesday we can pre-check with procurement and confirm a 45-day provisional hold.

—Laura
Laura Chen
VP Finance, Meridian Health
laura.chen@meridianhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0129

Laura / Tom / procurement team — attaching a first draft rate matrix and a short SOW summary to make the provisional-hold mechanics explicit. Key points in the attached Meridian_2028_RateMatrix_v1.xlsx (summary below):

- 12-month commitment options: three tiers (Base: current monthly avg; Growth: Base x1.5; Scale: Base x2.5). Higher commitments reduce per-token price in stepped bands.
- Conditional 60-day provisional price-hold from signature of the attached SOW-summary.pdf (we're open to moving to 45-75, defaulted to 60).
- Onboarding credit: one-time $25k credit applied to first invoice for usage spikes > 200% month-1 baseline.
- Burst ladder: for bursts up to 1.5x baseline, charge at blended committed rate; for 1.5–3.0x, add a 12–18% uplift depending on tier; >3.0x handled case-by-case.
- SLA note: for sustained burst >1.5x longer than 72 hours we'll commit to capacity prioritization and provide a runbook — Monica will include operational commitments in the SOW.

Quick ask: Laura, can procurement confirm that a 60-day provisional hold meets the 'time-bound' requirement? If procurement prefers 45 or 75 we'll update the sheet. Also please confirm the target discount band (you referenced 18–22%) so we can put exact numbers in the xlsx.

I attached: Meridian_2028_RateMatrix_v1.xlsx, SOW-summary.pdf.

If this looks directionally right I can convert the matrix into a clean redline-ready amendment that Legal can sign and we can generate a DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Sean

--

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@meridianhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-09T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meridian Health renewal — initial rate planning (ops notes)

Looping in operational context for the SLA and onboarding credit: we pulled a usage snapshot and attached usage_report_Q1_2027.csv. Observations: median burst events are short (hours) but there were three multi-day events tied to a pilot in Feb. If Meridian takes the Growth tier (1.5x) our internal cluster planning needs ~2 weeks lead time for reserved pool resizing; if they go Scale (~2.5x) it's ~5 weeks. That affects timeline for guaranteed capacity during a sustained surge.

Onboarding credit mechanics: ops recommends applying the $25k as a line-item credit on invoice 1 and as a buffer that only applies to overage charges (not recurring committed invoice). Also recommend a one-time performance review 30 days after go-live to validate the burst uplift behavior.

Notes captured in the CSV attachment. I'll be on standby for any clarification procurement needs.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwoodinference.com

Date: 2027-04-12T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meridian Health renewal — initial rate planning

Sean / Monica — thanks for the quick turnaround and for making the provisional-hold explicit. Procurement confirms a 60-day hold is acceptable provided the SOW contains the commitment schedule and the DocuSign envelope is issued before April 30. Finance also asked we include a conditional step-down: if usage remains below Base for 3 consecutive months we revert to a pre-agreed minimum spend floor for the remainder of the term (to protect committed capacity economics).

We reviewed the rate matrix and the 18–22% discount band would be acceptable at the Growth tier if the onboarding credit is included; Finance would prefer an explicit blended effective rate in the SOW. Could you produce a redline-ready amendment and a DocuSign envelope with the SOW and rate matrix by end of day Thursday? If all aligns, we can sign and use the 60-day hold to give us time for internal approvals.

Tom and procurement will be the signatories. Please send the DocuSign link and HubSpot deal update when ready.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.
Laura
